newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam Jan-Apr trade gap falls yr-on-yr 30.2 pct.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam Jan-Apr trade gap falls yr-on-yr 30.2 pct.

text.p: Vietnam recorded a trade deficit of $962 million in the first four months of this year, 30.2 percent lower than in the same period of 1996, General Statistics Office figures showed on Monday.

The deficit in the first three months of this year was $762 million, but despite a slowdown in import growth the trade ministry has forecast a trade gap of more than $1.0 billion in the second quarter.

The statistics office said that imports since the beginning of this year were $3.64 billion, a rise of 7.7 percent from the same period last year. Exports were put at $2.68 billion, a rise of 33.8 percent.
Exports by enterprises with foreign investment were $243.3 million in the January-April period, a year-on-year rise of 26.7 percent. Their imports were $732.0 million, up 38.1 percent.

The country exported 3.29 million tonnes of crude oil in the first four months of the year, 21.4 percent more than in the corresponding period of 1996. Imports of petroleum products was 1.99 million tonnes, up 1.8 percent.
Rice exports came to 813,600 tonnes, up 15.5 percent, while coffee exports rose 106.4 percent to 198,600 tonnes.
